name: Light Mouse Grey
lede: Light Mouse Grey is a warm, brownish grey, the library's lightened variant of [[mouse-grey]], and our archive finds it in roughly one painting in ten.

sections.title: A modifier on an existing name
sections.body: The nearest named colors on file are [[pale-quaker-drab]] and [[middle-grey]], at Ridgway's 1912 atlas places the hue at plate LI, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files the same block (block 63) as light brownish gray, about 5.9 units away in CIEDE2000 [1]. In Munsell notation it is a near-neutral N 6.0; measured in LCH it has lightness 61, chroma under 5 and hue 90 degrees, close to [[slate]] and [[silver]] but warmer than either [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive, a match appears in 1,398 of 23,781 paintings, about 5.9 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 835 [2]. That is ahead of 88 percent of our named colors [2]. It plays a light tone in 46 percent of its appearances [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 122 of 1,674 paintings, 7.3 percent of the 1,674 paintings (122 of them) we have from that century, about 1.8 times the archive's typical rate [2]. Shen Zhou is its most devoted painter, carrying it in 7 of his 12 archived works, 6.3 times the typical rate [2]. It shares canvases more than chance would predict with [[nickel]] and [[lilac-grey]] [2].

questions.q: Light Mouse Grey is built by adding "light" to which existing color name?
True or false: Light Mouse Grey appears most often in Norwegian paintings in our archive.

openers: Shen Zhou carries Light Mouse Grey in over half of his archived paintings, 6.3 times our archive's typical rate.

issues: Field notes overstated the painting count and role breakdown (claimed 2,310 paintings and 'highlight in 63%, mid-tone in another third'; real fieldnotes show 1,398/835 and light-tone 46% as the top role), the painter stat (claimed Shen Zhou 8/12; real is 7/12, 6.3x not ~7x), a fabricated 'Chinese paintings' claim with no supporting country data, and wrong companion colors (grey/silver; the real shared-canvas matches are Nickel and Lilac-Grey); corrected.
